title: Aviation Ordnance Systems Technician (SSgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN
raw_text:
4.     MOS 6541, Aviation Ordnance Systems Technician (SSgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC AVN

    a. Summary. Aviation Ordnance Systems Technicians perform duties
incident to the accounting, stowage, breakout, testing, maintenance,
assembly, and transportation of aircraft armament systems, munitions handling
equipment, air launched missiles, and conventional munitions. At the IMA
level, Aviation Ordnance System Technicians perform required inspections,
tests, checks, adjustments, preventive maintenance, and repair on armament
weapons support equipment (AWSE), missile launching equipment, multiple
ejection/triple ejection bomb racks, aircraft guns, turrets, aircraft crew-
served weapons, aerial targets, and a wide variety of highly technical
aircraft armament weapon systems in addition to performing quality assurance,
safety, and maintenance management duties.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a U.S. citizen.

            (2) Must have normal color perception.

            (3) Must possess a valid state driver's license.

            (4) Security requirement:     secret security clearance eligibility.

            (5) Must possess a CL score of 105 or GT score of 105 or higher.

        (6) Must meet the medical requirements for Explosives Handlers and
Explosives Vehicle Operators contained in Article 15-107 of reference (ai).

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete AO A1 Aviation Ordnance Course (N23G3U2) and the CNATT
AO (C) Course (M04G3M6 or M04G4C6) at CNATT MARU, Cherry Point, NC.



                                           3-423                        Enclosure (1)
 3143                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



            (2) At the first assigned unit, marines:

            (a) Must obtain appropriate support equipment and/or material
handling licensing upon initial unit assignment (Sgt to Pvt).

            (b) Marines who handle explosives must meet the criteria to be
qualified and certified as per reference (ay).

            (c) Must obtain incidental motor vehicle operator licensing for
tactical vehicles up to 7-ton MTVR (or equivalent).

            (d) Must complete incidental motor vehicle licensing for HMMWV
tactical vehicle.

            (e) Must complete incidental motor vehicle licensing for HMMWV
tactical vehicle and/or JLTV.

       d.   Duties

            (1) SSgt to Pvt:

            (a) Performs IMA level maintenance on armament weapons support
equipment (AWSE).

            (b) Assembles and performs maintenance on air-launched missiles,
and conventional munitions, as authorized.

            (c) Performs IMA level maintenance on aircraft armament systems
(aircraft armament equipment and aircraft gun systems).

            (d) Identifies munitions by type, nomenclature, and explosive
hazard. Identifies the hazard present and appropriate emergency response
procedures for each type of munitions handled.

            (e) Transports explosives utilizing assigned handling and
transportation equipment.

            (f) Employs appropriate safety precautions, security procedures,
and record keeping practices for munitions.

            (g) Conducts ammunition inventories and maintains stock records
of lots/serial numbers.

            (h) Performs operator tasks associated with Ordnance Information
System (OIS) Ammunition Accounting and Management System.

                (i) Perform IMA level maintenance on aircraft guns.

            (j) Performs inventory management tasks associated with the All
Weapons Information System (AWIS) website.

                (k) Prepares, packages and certifies hazardous material for
shipment.

                (l) Certifies vehicles for transport of hazardous materials.




                                        3-424                          Enclosure (1)
 3143                                                              NAVMC 1200.1L



           (2) SSgt to Cpl:

            (a) Maintains records and distinguishes the different
modifications on all models of missiles and conventional munitions assigned.

            (b) Utilizes available technical and supply publications to
obtain accurate and complete data for supply purposes.

            (c) Perform inspections on the maintenance, storage, and shipment
of explosives.

            (d) Using ammunition stock and allowance lists/publications,
prepares and edits ammunition requisitions and takes requisition follow-up
actions.

               (e) Makes ammunition issues, prepares invoices, and custody
records.

            (f) Maintains files, prepares naval messages, and submits
ammunition transactions.

            (g) Performs the System Administrator tasks associated with
Ordnance Information System (OIS) Ammunition Accounting and Management
System.

           (3) SSgt and Sgt:

               (a) Establishes a training program for aviation ordnance
technicians.

            (b) Perform functions in the establishment operations of a
conventional munitions storage area, advance base ammunition storage point,
ready storage areas and Forward Arming and Refueling Points (FARP).

            (c) Prepares conventional/ordnance deficiency reports, explosive
event reports, explosive mishap reports, technical publication deficiency
reports, product quality deficiency reports, missing lost stolen/recovered
ammunition reports, and engineering investigation requests, when appropriate.

            (d) Perform ammunition stock recording section functions/tasks
utilizing the ordnance information system (OIS).

            (e) Determine the serviceability of ammunition and perform
ammunition sentencing functions.

            (f) Establish and supervise the operation of a Forward Arming and
Refueling Point (FARP).

               (g) Supervise operations in an ammunition assembly area.

           (4) SSgt:

            (a) Utilizes aviation ordnance administrative procedures
necessary to establish and operate an IMA.

               (b) Conducts administrative and material inspections of IMA
activities.




                                       3-425                        Enclosure (1)
 3143                                                                     NAVMC 1200.1L



            (c) Prepares naval messages, orders, instructions, SOPs, and
safety precautions.

                (d) Manage the Ammunition Stock Recording System (ASRS).

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Explosive Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters 47-
5031.

            (2) Maintenance and Repair Workers, General 49-9042.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     Aircraft Ordnance Technician, 6531.
common_text: Aviation Ordnance MOSs handle Class V(A) ammunition issues from safety to procurement, storage, buildup, delivery, and subsequent aircraft loading and downloading. The OccFld includes both organizational and intermediate maintenance of aircraft weapon systems, aircraft guns, gun pods, aircraft crew-served weapons, bomb racks, missile launchers, and armament weapons support equipment (AWSE). Aviation Ordnance Marines are qualified and certified to handle Class V(A) munitions under current directives. Formal schooling is provided to Marines entering the OccFld. A wide variety of billet assignments are available as shown in the figure later in this entry. Marines entering the OccFld receive MOS 6500, Basic Aviation Ordnance Marine, and attend Aviation Ordnance, Class AO A1 School (N23G3U2) at Pensacola, Fl., with follow-on training at one of several CNATT AO(C) courses, dependent upon anticipated fleet assignment. Upon completion of the applicable AO(C) course, they are designated as either MOS 6531 Aircraft Ordnance Technician or MOS 6541 Aviation Ordnance Systems Technician and are assigned to a T/M/S flying squadron in the case of MOS 6531 or a Marine Aviation Logistics Squadron(MALS)/Station Weapons in the case of MOS 6541.

matches: Maintain, repair, and rebuild aircraft structures, functional components, and parts, such as wings and fuselage, rigging, hydraulic units, oxygen systems, fuel systems, electrical systems, gaskets, or seals.

The OccFld includes both organizational and intermediate maintenance of aircraft weapon systems, aircraft guns, gun pods, aircraft crew-served weapons, bomb racks, missile launchers, and armament weapons support equipment (AWSE).
Coordinate work with that of engineers, technicians, and other aircraft maintenance personnel.

Aviation Ordnance Systems Technicians perform duties incident to the accounting, stowage, breakout, testing, maintenance, assembly, and transportation of aircraft armament systems, munitions handling equipment, air launched missiles, and conventional munitions.
Perform maintenance tasks necessary to keep equipment working properly.
d. Duties (1) SSgt to Pvt: (a) Performs IMA level maintenance on armament weapons support equipment (AWSE).
Modify, devise, or maintain nuclear equipment used in operations.
(b) Assembles and performs maintenance on air-launched missiles, and conventional munitions, as authorized.
Inspect work of aircraft mechanics performing maintenance, modification, or repair and overhaul of aircraft and aircraft mechanical systems to ensure adherence to standards and procedures.
(c) Performs IMA level maintenance on aircraft armament systems (aircraft armament equipment and aircraft gun systems).
Determine types of bullets and specific weapons used in shootings.
(d) Identifies munitions by type, nomenclature, and explosive hazard.
Implement appropriate industrial emergency response procedures.
Identifies the hazard present and appropriate emergency response procedures for each type of munitions handled.
Drive trucks to transport explosives and blasting equipment to blasting sites.
(e) Transports explosives utilizing assigned handling and transportation equipment.
Move and store inventories of explosives, loaded perforating guns, and other materials, according to established safety procedures.
(f) Employs appropriate safety precautions, security procedures, and record keeping practices for munitions.
Locate and label parts, and maintain inventory of stock.
(g) Conducts ammunition inventories and maintains stock records of lots/serial numbers.

Operate office equipment, such as voice mail messaging systems, and use word processing, spreadsheet, or other software applications to prepare reports, invoices, financial statements, letters, case histories, or medical records.
(h) Performs operator tasks associated with Ordnance Information System (OIS) Ammunition Accounting and Management System.
Maintain repair logs, documenting all preventive and corrective aircraft maintenance.
(i) Perform IMA level maintenance on aircraft guns.
Establish and maintain inventory, records, or documentation systems.
(j) Performs inventory management tasks associated with the All Weapons Information System (AWIS) website.
Evaluate new methods of packaging, testing, shipping, or transporting hazardous materials to ensure adequate public safety protection.
(k) Prepares, packages and certifies hazardous material for shipment.
Evaluate new methods of packaging, testing, shipping, or transporting hazardous materials to ensure adequate public safety protection.
(l) Certifies vehicles for transport of hazardous materials.
Direct and support the compilation and analysis of technical source data necessary for product development.
(b) Utilizes available technical and supply publications to obtain accurate and complete data for supply purposes.
Inspect facilities and equipment for signs of disrepair, and perform necessary maintenance work.
(c) Perform inspections on the maintenance, storage, and shipment of explosives.
Requisition and issue equipment and supplies.
(d) Using ammunition stock and allowance lists/publications, prepares and edits ammunition requisitions and takes requisition follow-up actions.
Prepare invoices, shipping documents, and contracts.
(e) Makes ammunition issues, prepares invoices, and custody records.
Maintain records of daily activities, personnel reports, ship positions and movements, ports of call, weather and sea conditions, pollution control efforts, or cargo or passenger status.
(f) Maintains files, prepares naval messages, and submits ammunition transactions.
Perform general administrative tasks, such as answering telephones, scheduling appointments, and ordering supplies or equipment.
(g) Performs the System Administrator tasks associated with Ordnance Information System (OIS) Ammunition Accounting and Management System.
Analyze training programs and conduct oral and written examinations to ensure the competency of persons operating, installing, and repairing aircraft equipment.
(3) SSgt and Sgt: (a) Establishes a training program for aviation ordnance technicians.
Move and store inventories of explosives, loaded perforating guns, and other materials, according to established safety procedures.

(b) Perform functions in the establishment operations of a conventional munitions storage area, advance base ammunition storage point, ready storage areas and Forward Arming and Refueling Points (FARP).
Prepare reports documenting investigation activities and results.

(c) Prepares conventional/ordnance deficiency reports, explosive event reports, explosive mishap reports, technical publication deficiency reports, product quality deficiency reports, missing lost stolen/recovered ammunition reports, and engineering investigation requests, when appropriate.
Record operational information on specified production reports.
(d) Perform ammunition stock recording section functions/tasks utilizing the ordnance information system (OIS).
Determine types of bullets and specific weapons used in shootings.
(e) Determine the serviceability of ammunition and perform ammunition sentencing functions.
Supervise assemblers and train employees on job procedures.
(g) Supervise operations in an ammunition assembly area.
Coordinate with agencies to meet aircrew requirements for billeting, messing, refueling, ground transportation, and transient aircraft maintenance.
(4) SSgt: (a) Utilizes aviation ordnance administrative procedures necessary to establish and operate an IMA.
Conduct routine and special inspections as required by regulations.
(b) Conducts administrative and material inspections of IMA activities.
Relay messages about emergencies, accidents, locations of crew and personnel, and fire hazard conditions.
(c) Prepares naval messages, orders, instructions, SOPs, and safety precautions.
Establish and maintain inventory, records, or documentation systems.
(d) Manage the Ammunition Stock Recording System (ASRS).

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
